comparison: Perfect agreement on study design and methodology claims (C1, C13, C68, C71-C79, C84). Both evaluations rate these as SUPPORTED, recognizing the value of this study in addressing genetic diversity gaps in COVID-19 research and accepting the methodological approach without concerns.

Significant disagreement on BAZ2B locus (C2, C18-C21, C35-C37, C81-C82). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on statistical significance and functional annotation, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN due to lack of independent replication cohort and failure to replicate in trans-ancestry meta-analysis (C40), raising concerns about false positives.

Disagreement on DDIAS locus (C22, C38, C83). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED despite fine mapping convergence issues, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN citing the same replication concerns as BAZ2B and the fine mapping failure as additional evidence of uncertainty.

Agreement on CREBBP locus (C3, C45). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes genome-wide significance and cross-population nature, while peer reviewers explicitly recognize this as a key strength with biological plausibility from functional evidence (C65-C67).

Disagreement on eQTL evidence (C27-C29, C55-C58). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on effect sizes and tissue specificity, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN due to concerns that GTEx eQTL data are predominantly from European ancestries, questioning applicability to admixed American populations.

Disagreement on TWAS findings (C30-C34, C59-C62). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on statistical significance and tissue specificity, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN noting that TWAS models were predominantly trained on European samples and lack independent replication.

Agreement on replication of known loci (C24-C25, C39, C41-C44). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the high replication rate and additional associations, while peer reviewers accept these results as validation of study methodology and quality control.

Disagreement on PGS performance (C46-C49). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on effect sizes and variance explained metrics, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN citing concerns about arbitrary variant selection and modest variance explained (1.07%).

OpenEval rates the suggestive association at C23 as UNCERTAIN due to marginal p-value (6.11×10⁻⁸) not reaching genome-wide significance threshold. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific claim.

Partial overlap on replication claims (C24-C26). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses replication and lack of comorbidity associations, while peer reviewers focus on broader replication results including additional loci (C39, C41-C44).

Agreement on biological interpretation (C50-C54). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate citations and plausible mechanisms, while peer reviewers accept the literature-based contextualization but note lack of experimental validation, treating these as hypotheses.

Partial overlap on biological context for cross-population genes (C63-C67). OpenEval rates biological context as SUPPORTED with well-cited mechanisms. Peer reviewers incorporate these claims into their SUPPORTED evaluation of CREBBP, accepting the functional evidence.

Partial overlap on biological context (C63-C64). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for cross-population gene mechanisms. Peer reviewers include these in their broader acceptance of biological interpretation, noting standard GWAS practice but lack of experimental validation.

Related to study rationale (C4-C12). OpenEval rates background context as SUPPORTED with proper citations. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this rationale through their recognition of the study's value in addressing genetic diversity gaps, though they evaluate the broader study design rather than specific background claims.

Agreement on quality control (C80). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the low lambda value (1.015) as evidence of appropriate population stratification control, while peer reviewers accept the methodological approach and state-of-the-art statistical genomics methods.

Peer reviewers explicitly evaluate the negative replication result for BAZ2B in trans-ancestry meta-analysis (C40) as SUPPORTED, demonstrating population-specific nature. OpenEval includes C40 in R2 evaluation but does not separately evaluate this negative result.
